title: Remove the deprecated task time-budget UI from both IDE clients
description: packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts marks the task time-budget fields DEPRECATED and ignored (the 80%/100% warn feature was removed), but the clients still advertise it: moe-jetbrains MoeBundle.properties has 'moe.metrics.budgetRemaining=Budget remaining' (Metrics + Budget surface), and moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts:726-770 renders task.budget.wallClockMs as 'remaining'. Users see a control that does nothing. Remove the budget rendering and strings from both clients (keep chat hop limits and reopen caps — those are separate and live), drop any dead budget fields from the plugin Task/Metrics models, and scrub docs/CONFIGURATION.md + docs/SCHEMA.md of budget as a live setting (leave the deprecation note in schema.ts). Source: roadmap 2026-09-10 §4 'Effective settings'.
definitionOfDone: No 'budget' string remains in moe-jetbrains/src/main (grep), MetricsPanel compiles without the budget KPI
TaskDetailPanel.ts no longer reads task.budget; npm run compile green
docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/SCHEMA.md do not present time budgets as a live setting
./gradlew test green and moe-vscode npm test green

implementationPlan.description: RED FIRST: A DOC-CONTRACT GUARD THAT FAILS ON TODAY'S DOCS. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/util/taskTimeBudgetDocs.test.ts, a vitest file that reads docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/SCHEMA.md off disk and asserts the documented contract matches the daemon's actual behavior. Resolve the repository root from import.meta.url through fileURLToPath the way src/tools/registry.test.ts resolves its own directory, and fail with a clear message if a file is missing rather than silently passing - that is this test's own error handling, and a guard that passes when it cannot find its input is worse than no guard. Anchor the assertions on specific terms instead of vague prose matching: every line mentioning pacePerStepMs, and every line describing the task time-budget field or its interface, must also carry a deprecation marker on the same line or in its immediately adjacent annotation, and no line may state that a submission SEEDS a budget or that the daemon CHECKS a cap. Add the positive half, which is what keeps this guard from becoming a blunt search-and-destroy: assert the chat hop limit and the reopen cap are still documented AND still unmarked as deprecated, so a later over-eager cleanup that scrubs live settings fails here. Run it now against unmodified docs - Windows `npm --prefix packages/moe-daemon test -- src/util/taskTimeBudgetDocs.test.ts`, remembering npm.cmd if the PowerShell policy blocks the shim - and save the failing output. It must fail on the seeding sentence in CONFIGURATION.md, which is the recorded proof that the docs really did advertise a removed feature.

CORRECT docs/CONFIGURATION.md. Rewrite the pacePerStepMs row at line 168 so it describes what the daemon actually does today: the setting is retained for compatibility and is ignored, and no task time budget is seeded from it, because the warn feature it fed was removed. Keep the row rather than deleting it - the key can still appear in a real project file, so a reader who finds it needs to learn it does nothing, which a silent deletion would not tell them. Mark it clearly deprecated using whatever convention the surrounding table already uses, and drop the default and range presentation that implies a live tunable. Change nothing else in the file: every other setting row, and in particular the chat hop limit and the reopen cap, stay exactly as they are, since those are live and the guard test now asserts they remain unmarked. No behavior change and no daemon edit in this step.

CORRECT docs/SCHEMA.md. Three edits, all of the same kind. At lines 180-181 remove the claim that a submission seeds the task budget from pacePerStepMs and mark the field deprecated and ignored, matching the wording chosen for CONFIGURATION.md so the two documents agree. At line 437 change the task budget member's annotation from presenting a soft wall-clock cap to stating it is a deprecated legacy field the daemon ignores, and keep the member documented, because legacy records on disk and older clients on the wire still carry it and a reader needs to know it is accepted but inert. At lines 742-746 rewrite the interface description so it no longer says the daemon checks firstClaimAt plus the cap - that check was removed - while still describing the legacy shape for anyone reading an old record. Do not touch the daemon's own DEPRECATED notes in packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts, do not change any persisted data or wire compatibility, and do not touch the planRevision section a sibling task added. Leave the reopen and chat limits alone.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Deleting the pacePerStepMs row and the legacy field from the documents outright - rejected: the key can still appear in a real project file and the field still appears in legacy records and older client payloads, so a reader needs to be told it is accepted and inert rather than left to wonder why it is undocumented. Writing the guard as a blunt search for the retired word - rejected: it would fire on the live reopen cap and require carve-outs that rot; anchoring on pacePerStepMs and on the specific field and interface, plus asserting the live settings stay unmarked, is both stricter and safer. Putting the guard in a client test suite - rejected: the contract being asserted is the daemon's behavior versus its documentation, and the daemon suite already has a precedent for tests that read repository files. Finishing any client removal here if a child fell short - rejected: it would duplicate child work, break the file scope and weaken their tests; report the gap to the child instead.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured live on 2026-09-11, and the defect is exactly as the breakdown described: the daemon's own schema marks the task time-budget fields deprecated and ignored, while both documents still describe the feature as active. CONFIGURATION.md:168 states that a plan submission seeds an absent task budget from pacePerStepMs and presents a default and a valid range, which reads as a live tunable. SCHEMA.md repeats the seeding claim at 180-181, annotates the field as a soft wall-clock cap at 437, and at 742-746 says the daemon checks firstClaimAt plus the cap - a check that no longer exists. Two near-misses must survive the cleanup: schema.ts:740 refers to a reopen budget, which is the live reopen cap, and the chat hop limit is also live, so a blunt search-and-destroy over the word would damage real documentation. That is why the guard test has a positive half asserting both remain documented and unmarked. One correction to the task prose, already noted by the breakdown: MetricsPanel needs no edit - the JetBrains remaining-versus-cap readout lives in TaskDetailDialog and the board badge, and both belong to the first child. This parent verifies the client greps rather than performing any client edit, so its own diff is two documents and one new test.
planningNotes.risks: All three children were unlanded when this plan was written, so step 1 must block rather than proceed on assumption - and the parent must never finish a child's removal itself. The guard test is the piece most likely to be built wrong in two opposite ways: too loose and it passes on the current docs, too blunt and it condemns the live reopen and chat settings; the red run in step 2 proves the first, and the positive assertions prove the second. Do not touch the daemon's schema notes, persisted data or wire compatibility - an old record carrying the legacy field must still load. docs/SCHEMA.md is contended: a sibling added a planRevision section to it, so re-read before editing and leave that section alone. Gradle output is shared infrastructure - serialize it and treat an UP-TO-DATE result as no test run. Run the full daemon suite once as well as the focused file, or a test that is never collected by the normal run will look green while guarding nothing. Finally, the two documents must agree with each other after the edit, not just each be individually defensible.
